thread:
incident-bot: PAGER: multi-GPU collective stall detected on cluster-gamma (tp4 job runner). Auto-page to oncall (alice.kim). Severity: P1. Symptoms: requests stuck, kube probe flapping, container restarts.

alice.kim: on it, joining bridge. seeing 503s in the customer-facing inference route. marking as page. @bob.chen can you grab nvtop / dmesg once i give node id? :eyes:

bob.chen: roger, ping me node when you have it. I can tail logs and grab GPU state.

carla.ops: FYI we have had two node flaps in the last 6h in the same rack; infra alerted earlier but didnt escalate. I've raised a ticket to check hardware.

alice.kim: root node is gpu-node-17 (ephemeral). attaching short log excerpt from agent: ```[2025-03-12T21:03:12Z] nccl: ERROR Timeout waiting for all ranks to be ready
[2025-03-12T21:03:12Z] torch.distributed: Rendezvous timed out
[2025-03-12T21:03:15Z] containerd: container exited with status 137 (OOM)```

dmitri.ml: Timeout + OOM pattern suggests memory pressure during pipeline parallel allreduce; could be KV-cache blowup from long prefixes, or stray microbatch size. What model/shape?

alice.kim: This is hosted-inference model: tp4-bert-large-ish, seqlen ~ 2048, batch 1 but internal microbatching for pipeline parallel. Recent traffic spike from client A.

dmitri.ml: okay. immediate mitigations: 1) drain new requests from that node, 2) scale down pipeline parallelism for running replicas if we can, 3) fallback to a single-GPU quantized variant if available.

carla.ops: draining node now, setting cordon on gpu-node-17. ``kubectl cordon gpu-node-17 && kubectl drain gpu-node-17 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data --grace-period=30``

bob.chen: nvtop shows GPU mem at ~97% right before crash. dmesg has a CUDA Xid 79 line and then process killed by OOM killer. grabbing container logs and NCCL debug trace.

alice.kim: Starting canary fallback route: switching production-route v2 -> v1 (quantized) for 10% traffic to reduce impact. @eva-support can you post a customer update for tenant ID 8432 that we are investigating degraded latency? keep it short. :speech_balloon:

eva-support: Drafting: "We are investigating a service degradation affecting a subset of inference requests. Engineers are actively mitigating and a partial rollback is in progress to restore capacity. We will update in 30 minutes or sooner." Want me to send now?

alice.kim: yes send. Note customer impact: some requests returned 503 or hung for ~30s; no data loss reported.

pagerbot: bridge created: https://meet.bridge/infra/3490000123 - incident channel pinned. Auto-runbook: /runbooks/tp-collective-hang.md attached.

dmitri.ml: quick triage notes: NCCL reports communicator reset after rank 1 lost connection -> suspected node-level preemption or container OOM; pipeline allreduce couldn't recover. Two helpful quick experiments: 1) restart communicator (not great in prod), 2) force-redeploy replicas with reduced microbatch size and enable prefix cache eviction to avoid KV blowup.

carla.ops: I can restart the kubelet on gpu-node-17 but prefer to reprovision a fresh node to avoid noisy neighbor effects. starting reprovision now.

bob.chen: collected core dumps and /var/log/nvidia-installer.log, uploading to S3: s3://redwood-debug/3490000123/gpu-node-17/ . I've redacted customer payloads.

alice.kim: decision: 1) keep node cordoned and replace (carla) 2) route 50% traffic to quantized fallback while we observe (alice) 3) roll new replicas with reduced microbatch and enable model-level kv_cache.max_entries=20000 (dmitri to produce patch) 4) open followup with infra for hardware check.

dmitri.ml: pushing a hotfix to runtime config: ```env: MODEL_MICROBATCH=1 KV_CACHE_MAX_ENTRIES=20000 NCCL_TIMEOUT_SEC=120``` rolling to canary pool now.

alice.kim: canary looks stable at 10% -> 50% routing. latency improved ~2x on quantized variant, error rate down to 1.2% from 8.5%. monitoring for 10m window.

eva-support: update posted to customer and status page. customer rep replied: "Thanks, please advise ETA for full restoration" — suggested ETA: 45-60m pending node replace and full rollout.

carla.ops: reprovision complete, new node gpu-node-23 ready and joined cluster. kubelet logs show clean startup.

bob.chen: redeploying pods back into service on new node with updated env. watching metrics.

dmitri.ml: after restart, NCCL errors not present in new replicas. hypothesize combination of memory fragmentation + repeated container restarts produced inconsistent communicator state leading to timeout. will follow up with an eval to reproduce locally.

alice.kim: summarizing action items: - Replace gpu-node-17 (carla) - Hotfix runtime env to reduce microbatch and limit kv cache (dmitri) - Keep quantized fallback route at 50% until error rate <0.5% for 30m (alice) - Customer comms: EVa to keep updated (eva-support) - Infra follow-up ticket for rack flapping (carla)

alice.kim: handing off to night oncall @bob.chen for post-incident monitoring. I'll update the incident log and create postmortem template.

bob.chen: taking over monitoring. I'll alert if error rate >1% or new Xid appears.

incident-bot: INCIDENT STATUS: degraded -> mitigated (partial). Next update scheduled in 30m. Incident ticket: #INC-2025-3490000123.

alice.kim: thanks everyone. adding note: consider adding automatic KV cache eviction for long-prefix workloads as a mitigation knob for future.

carla.ops: filing infra ticket: INFRA-3490 referencing node serial and rack telemetry.

bob.chen: attaching short diagnostic snippet for postmortem: ```$ nvidia-smi --query-gpu=memory.used,memory.total --format=csv -l 1
memory.used [MiB], memory.total [MiB]
24030 MiB, 24576 MiB```

dmitri.ml: will run a local repro with slightly smaller microbatch and stress test NCCL timeout.

eva-support: customer update sent, they acknowledged. closing comm loop.

alice.kim: incident transitioned to mitigated, creating draft postmortem. If anyone has extra logs or notes drop them here. :heart:
